chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the silk mattress and the like of it from brocade, and the silk prayer mat and the like of it from brocade, is it permissible for the man to sleep on it, recline upon it, and pray? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He may spread it out, stand upon it, but not prostrate upon it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for men to prostrate on silk or brocade during prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) delineates the permissibility of silk for men by distinguishing between its use as a surface for resting or standing versus the act of prostration, which requires direct contact with the earth or permissible materials. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that the prohibition on men wearing silk does not extend to all forms of contact, but specifically restricts the ritual act of sujood on it to maintain the humility and distinctiveness of the prayer posture.
